questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which process breaks large food molecules into smaller absorbable units?
questions.answer: Digestion

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Differentiate ingestion and absorption.
questions.answer: Ingestion is taking food into the body; absorption is the movement of digested nutrients into blood or lymph.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe the major stages by which food is processed and nutrients become available to body cells.
questions.answer: Award 1 mark each for ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation/use by cells, and egestion of undigested material.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Where does most nutrient absorption occur?
questions.answer: Small intestine

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State one function of the stomach and one of the small intestine.
questions.answer: The stomach mixes food and begins important digestion; the small intestine completes much digestion and absorbs most nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how the structure and functions of the alimentary canal support digestion and absorption.
questions.answer: Award marks for sequential transport, mechanical/chemical digestion, enzyme action, absorption surface, and movement of nutrients into circulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which structure is the main site of gas exchange in the lungs?
questions.answer: Alveoli

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why are alveoli suitable for gas exchange?
questions.answer: They provide a large, thin, moist surface with a rich blood supply, allowing rapid diffusion of gases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain inhalation, exhalation and gas exchange in the human respiratory system.
questions.answer: Award marks for rib/diaphragm changes during inhalation, pressure/volume change, reverse changes during exhalation, alveolar diffusion, and blood transport of gases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: During inhalation, what happens to the diaphragm?
questions.answer: It contracts and flattens

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: How does contraction of the diaphragm help air enter the lungs?
questions.answer: Contraction flattens the diaphragm, increasing thoracic volume and lowering pressure so air moves into the lungs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Compare inhalation and exhalation in terms of muscle action, thoracic volume and pressure.
questions.answer: Award marks for diaphragm action, rib movement, volume change, pressure change, and resulting direction of airflow.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which blood component is mainly responsible for oxygen transport?
questions.answer: Red blood cells

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State one function each of red blood cells and platelets.
questions.answer: Red blood cells transport oxygen; platelets help blood clot.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe the major components of blood and explain how each supports transport or protection.
questions.answer: Award marks for plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and an accurate function for each.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which chamber pumps oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation?
questions.answer: Left ventricle

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle?
questions.answer: It must generate higher pressure to pump blood through the whole body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Trace blood flow through the four chambers of the heart and the pulmonary/systemic circuits.
questions.answer: Award marks for right atrium, right ventricle to lungs, return to left atrium, left ventricle to body, and correct valve/major-vessel direction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the functional unit of the kidney?
questions.answer: Nephron

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is selective reabsorption in a nephron?
questions.answer: It is the return of useful substances such as glucose, needed ions and much water from the filtrate to the blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how filtration, selective reabsorption and secretion contribute to urine formation.
questions.answer: Award marks for filtration, useful-substance reabsorption, water/ion regulation, secretion of selected wastes/ions, and formation of final urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which tube carries urine from a kidney to the urinary bladder?
questions.answer: Ureter

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Differentiate the ureter and urethra.
questions.answer: A ureter carries urine from a kidney to the bladder; the urethra carries urine from the bladder to the outside.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe the pathway of urine from its formation in the kidneys to elimination.
questions.answer: Award marks for nephron formation, collecting ducts/renal pelvis, ureters, bladder storage, and urethral elimination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Neurons - The Units of Nervous System
questions.question_text: Which part of a neuron normally carries impulses away from the cell body?
questions.answer: Axon
tags: Neurons - The Units of Nervous System

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Neurons - The Units of Nervous System
questions.question_text: State the roles of dendrites and axon.
questions.answer: Dendrites receive signals toward the cell body; the axon carries impulses away from the cell body.
tags: Neurons - The Units of Nervous System

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Neurons - The Units of Nervous System
questions.question_text: Explain how a nervous response can pass from receptor to effector.
questions.answer: Award marks for receptor, sensory neuron, central processing/relay, motor neuron, and effector response.
tags: Neurons - The Units of Nervous System

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Hormones are released into which transport medium?
questions.answer: Blood

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: How does endocrine coordination differ from nervous coordination?
questions.answer: Endocrine control uses hormones carried in blood and is often slower/longer lasting; nervous control uses electrical impulses and is usually faster/more targeted.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Compare nervous and endocrine coordination using signal type, route, speed, duration and target specificity.
questions.answer: Award one mark for each accurate comparison of signal, route, speed, duration and targeting.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is fertilization?

options.text: Fusion of male and female gametes

questions.answer: Fusion of male and female gametes

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why are gametes haploid?
questions.answer: They contain one set of chromosomes so fertilization restores the diploid chromosome number rather than doubling it each generation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how gamete formation and fertilization maintain chromosome number across generations.
questions.answer: Award marks for meiosis, haploid gametes, fusion at fertilization, diploid zygote restoration, and genetic variation/parental contribution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Role of Hormones in Sexual Development
questions.question_text: Which general role do reproductive hormones have during puberty?

options.text: They regulate development of reproductive organs and secondary sexual characteristics

questions.answer: They regulate development of reproductive organs and secondary sexual characteristics
tags: Role of Hormones in Sexual Development

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Role of Hormones in Sexual Development
questions.question_text: State one reason hormonal regulation is important in reproduction.
questions.answer: Hormones coordinate development and timing of reproductive functions such as gamete production and reproductive cycles.
tags: Role of Hormones in Sexual Development

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Role of Hormones in Sexual Development
questions.question_text: Describe how hormonal signals coordinate major reproductive changes during adolescence and adulthood.
questions.answer: Award marks for endocrine source, target tissues, puberty changes, gamete/reproductive function regulation, and feedback/coordination concept.
tags: Role of Hormones in Sexual Development

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What molecule carries most hereditary information in chromosomes?
questions.answer: DNA

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Define a gene in relation to DNA.
questions.answer: A gene is a functional segment of DNA that carries information contributing to a biological product or inherited characteristic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Relate chromosomes, DNA and genes to the transmission of hereditary information.
questions.answer: Award marks for chromosomes containing DNA, DNA structure/information role, genes as DNA segments, replication/transmission, and inheritance through gametes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What term describes alternative forms of the same gene?
questions.answer: Alleles

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Differentiate genotype and phenotype.
questions.answer: Genotype is the allele combination/genetic constitution; phenotype is the observable characteristic produced by genotype together with environmental effects.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain a simple monohybrid inheritance pattern using alleles, dominance, genotype and phenotype.
questions.answer: Award marks for allele symbols, parental genotypes, gametes, offspring genotype combinations, and correct phenotype interpretation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Genetic engineering directly involves what?

options.text: Deliberate modification or transfer of genetic material

questions.answer: Deliberate modification or transfer of genetic material

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is meant by genetic engineering?
questions.answer: It is the deliberate manipulation of genetic material to introduce, remove or alter genetic information for a desired purpose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe a general sequence by which a useful gene can be identified, transferred and expressed in a host organism.
questions.answer: Award marks for gene identification/isolation, vector or delivery method, insertion into host, selection/verification, and expression/use of the product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which is an example of biotechnology?

options.text: Using microorganisms or engineered cells to make useful products

questions.answer: Using microorganisms or engineered cells to make useful products

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State one benefit and one potential concern associated with biotechnology.
questions.answer: A benefit can be production of medicines or improved crops; a concern can involve environmental, ethical or biosafety risks that require assessment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Evaluate biotechnology by describing two applications, two potential benefits and one risk-management consideration.
questions.answer: Award marks for two valid applications, two relevant benefits, and one thoughtful risk/biosafety/ethical consideration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A pathogen is best defined as what?
questions.answer: A disease-causing biological agent

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name two broad types of pathogens.
questions.answer: Examples include viruses, bacteria, fungi and protozoan parasites; any two valid groups earn credit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how pathogens cause disease and how transmission can be reduced.
questions.answer: Award marks for pathogen entry, multiplication/action, host damage or symptoms, transmission route, and a matching prevention/control method.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of an immune response?

options.text: To recognize and control harmful foreign agents

questions.answer: To recognize and control harmful foreign agents

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Differentiate innate and adaptive immunity.
questions.answer: Innate immunity provides rapid non-specific defenses; adaptive immunity develops specific responses and can generate immunological memory.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Compare innate and adaptive immunity and explain how vaccination can strengthen protection.
questions.answer: Award marks for innate features, adaptive specificity, lymphocyte/antibody or cellular response concept, memory, and vaccination stimulating protective memory without causing the full disease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Theory of Evolution by Natural Selection
questions.question_text: Natural selection acts most directly on what?

options.text: Heritable variation affecting survival or reproduction

questions.answer: Heritable variation affecting survival or reproduction
tags: Theory of Evolution by Natural Selection

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Theory of Evolution by Natural Selection
questions.question_text: What role does variation play in natural selection?
questions.answer: Heritable variation creates differences among individuals; variants that improve survival or reproduction can become more common over generations.
tags: Theory of Evolution by Natural Selection

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Theory of Evolution by Natural Selection
questions.question_text: Explain natural selection from variation to change in a population over generations.
questions.answer: Award marks for heritable variation, environmental selection pressure, differential survival/reproduction, inheritance of advantageous variants, and changing trait/allele frequencies over generations.
tags: Theory of Evolution by Natural Selection

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which type of evidence can support common ancestry?
questions.answer: Comparative anatomy and molecular similarities

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State two kinds of evidence used to study evolution.
questions.answer: Examples include fossils, comparative anatomy, embryological patterns, biogeography and molecular/DNA similarities; any two valid forms earn credit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how multiple independent lines of evidence can support evolutionary relationships.
questions.answer: Award marks for fossil evidence, anatomical/homologous evidence, molecular/DNA evidence, biogeography or embryology, and synthesis showing agreement among independent evidence sources.
